svg.title: Space Flight Software: Layers & Trust Boundaries
svg.desc: An illustrative cFS-like spacecraft software stack separates mission-specific apps, executive services, OS abstractions, platform drivers and onboard hardware, with secured updates and bounded hardware authority.

g.text: Space Flight Software: Layers & Trust Boundaries
NASA cFS is one example; actual spacecraft architectures and RTOS choices vary by mission.
Payload, guidance, power or thermal tasks; validate required permissions
cFE-like messaging, events, tables and task lifecycle; enforce policy at appropriate boundaries
OSAL / RTEMS / VxWorks / Linux or mission-selected executive; capabilities vary
BSP, buses, device interfaces, hardware watchdogs and memory protection where available
Processor, avionics, radios and constrained power resources
Authenticate software updates and spacecraft commands separately
Application signatures, anti-rollback, link-layer security and memory isolation depend on the actual mission.
Conceptual separation following NASA cFS architecture terms; not a claim all missions implement cFE or a specific RTOS.
